problem: Embodied AI benchmarks such as navigation, instruction following and EQA mostly assume a static environment, so the agent cannot change object states. Classical rearrangement planning in robotics assumes perfect perception, planar or static setups, the same environment for training and test, or few object categories. No visually rich benchmark existed for rearranging objects from raw egocentric input in unseen rooms.
motivation: Interacting with and changing the environment is essential for embodied agents, and it cannot be studied in static environments. Rearrangement (Batra et al. 2020) is a broad task that subsumes several skills: navigation, spotting visual differences, reasoning about object state, pre/post-conditions of actions, and memory. The authors instantiate it in AI2-THOR at scale and show that the then state-of-the-art embodied-RL recipes largely fail on it.
key_idea: The paper defines the two-stage Room Rearrangement task: in the walkthrough stage the agent observes the goal room; in the unshuffle stage it must restore up to 5 moved or opened/closed objects from egocentric RGB. It releases the RoomR dataset (6,000 episodes, 120 AI2-THOR rooms) with IoU- and energy-based metrics, plus actor-critic baselines trained with DD-PPO and DAgger that use image-comparison or semantic-map-comparison memory.
insight: (1) Pure reward-based RL (PPO) gets stuck in local optima: PPO agents move very few objects (#Changed ≈0.3). They mostly place those correctly, keeping %E just under 1. IL/DAgger agents move more objects but tend to raise the scene energy (%E > 1). (2) An ImageNet-pretrained frozen ResNet18 beats the 3-layer 'Simple' CNN under IL on Success and %FixedStrict across all splits (e.g. test SR 2.8 vs 1.8); results are mixed under PPO. (3) Swapping the non-parametric image memory for a pretrained Active-Neural-SLAM semantic map improves generalization most: 1-Phase val %FixedStrict rises from 5.0 to 11.1 and test Success from 2.8 to 3.2. The authors caveat that parameter counts are not balanced. (4) The 2-Phase task is far harder (test SR 0.2–0.3) even though its training-set curves approach the 1-Phase IL models. The authors attribute the gap to learning dynamics and non-exhaustive walkthrough exploration, so comparative memory and exploration are the bottleneck.
method: Task formalization: each rigid object has state s_i=(pose in SE(3), openness in [0,1] or ∅, 3D box corners, broken flag). The walkthrough stage (max 250 steps) shows the goal state s*; after it, 1–5 objects are changed (N∈{0,1} openable non-pickupable objects plus M pickupable objects moved) to give s0; the unshuffle stage must restore s*.

Metrics: Success (all objects approximately equal: IoU≥0.5 for pickupable, |Δopenness|≤0.2 for openable). %FixedStrict = fraction of initially misplaced objects fixed, and 0 if any correctly placed object gets disturbed. %Energy Remaining = end energy / start energy under a distance/IoU-based energy D. #Changed = number of objects moved.

RoomR dataset: 120 iThor rooms (30 each of kitchen, living, bedroom, bathroom), split 80/20/20 train/val/test rooms, 50 rearrangements per room (4000/1000/1000). Uses 72 rearrangeable object types (62 pickupable, 10 openable non-pickupable); background objects are also shuffled per episode.

Actor-critic policy: frozen ImageNet ResNet18 (7×7×512 features) plus discrete-input embeddings feed a 1-layer 512-unit LSTM, with separate walkthrough and unshuffle policy heads (84 actions) and value heads.

Non-parametric map with image comparison: stores walkthrough RGB frames with their poses. During unshuffle it retrieves the frame saved at the pose nearest the current pose and compares it with the current view via attention. A 1-layer GRU also builds an implicit walkthrough encoding, frozen after walkthrough and fed back into the LSTM.

ANM semantic-mapping variant: an Active Neural SLAM mapper, pretrained to output a 40×40×75 egocentric semantic map (2m×2m; 3 free-space channels plus 72 object channels), then frozen. It replaces the image memory: walkthrough and unshuffle maps are concatenated, embedded by a CNN, and spatially attention-pooled to a 512-d vector that is input to the LSTM.

Hybrid training (AllenAct, ~75M steps): DD-PPO in the walkthrough stage with a reward for seeing new objects plus an end reward for the fraction of objects seen. DAgger imitation of a greedy heuristic expert with privileged GT state is used in the unshuffle stage; the expert-forcing probability is annealed to 0 over 1M steps (1-Phase) or 5M steps (2-Phase). PPO-only variants instead use the energy-decrease reward.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (ImageNet-pretrained, frozen) + 1-layer 512-unit LSTM (+GRU walkthrough encoder), trained from scratch with DD-PPO / DAgger; ANM variants add a pretrained, frozen Active Neural SLAM semantic mapper; 'Simple' variants use a 3-block CNN
setting.training_data: RoomR training split: 4000 rearrangements in 80 AI2-THOR rooms, ~75M environment steps per model. IL uses on-policy expert labels (DAgger) from a heuristic expert with GT scene and object state. The ANM mapper is pretrained on AI2-THOR semantic mapping for the 72 object categories.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 224×224 (90° FOV) + AgentPosition (perfect egomotion relative to start); the 1-Phase task adds a pixel-aligned WalkthroughRGB image of the goal configuration, the 2-Phase task adds an InWalkthrough flag
setting.action_space: 84 discrete high-level actions: MoveAhead/Left/Right/Back 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 90°, LookUp/Down 30°, Stand/Crouch, Pickup<Type> (62 types), Open<Type> (10 types; sets openness to its goal value), PlaceObject (snaps to the goal pose if the goal is visible and within 1.5 m, otherwise a heuristic drop), Done
setting.privileged: perfect agent pose (AgentPosition sensor). High-level Open/PlaceObject actions use goal-state knowledge (openness set to its goal value; the object snaps to its goal pose when visible and within 1.5 m). In 1-Phase, an aligned rendered goal-configuration image (WalkthroughRGB) at every step. No GT object locations for the learned policies.

RoomR is also known as the AI2-THOR Rearrangement Challenge (2021 version).
results: All learned baselines are near floor. The best 1-Phase model (RN18+ANM, IL) reaches 5.2 / 3.2 Success and 11.1 / 8.9 %FixedStrict on val/test, versus 1.7 / 2.8 and 5.0 / 6.3 for the RN18 IL model without semantic mapping. The 2-Phase agents reach only 0.3 test Success at best (RN18+ANM, PPO+IL; %FS 1.4). A GT-state heuristic expert solves 83.4% of test episodes. The best training-set Success is just 8.2% (1-Phase RN18 IL), so the task was far beyond the then state of the art.
limitations: Heavily abstracted actions: Open sets openness directly to its goal value, and PlaceObject snaps the object to its goal pose when the goal is visible within 1.5 m. Perfect egomotion is given, and moved objects are never hidden inside receptacles, so results say little about real manipulation.
The metric uses 3D-box IoU≥0.5, which ignores orientation. The benchmark assumes no duplicate object instances and single-room scenes only.
The ANM gains are called preliminary: parameter counts are not balanced. Only in-house baselines are compared, and learned policies remain close to chance (test Success ≤3.2%).
